title: Centrum Caspia: shop offices with two ground floors.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #456 | CENTRUM CASPIA, CAMERON HIGHLANDS
excerpt: Just 24 individual-title shop offices in the 87-acre Cameron Centrum township, built into a slope so each has two ground floors. Sean likes the design and the freedom from maintenance fees, but questions the visibility and how long tourist-level rents will last.
takeaways: Each shop office has two ground floors, one facing the front and one facing the back.
Intermediate lots ask about RM3.1 million and corner lots about RM7 million, with no maintenance fees.
Only 24 units, no view from the main road, and rents that depend on Cameron Highlands' crowds.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Centrum Caspia is 24 individual-title shop offices, the only ones in the township that don't come with a maintenance fee or the group's rules on signage. They are built into the slope so each has two ground floors: one at the front on the lower level and another opening onto the back on the level above, with a third storey on top.

Sean looked at the intermediate Type A, 20 by 95 ft and 4,461 sq ft, with two toilets and a wash area. Intermediate lots ask about RM3.1 million and the bigger corner lots about RM7 million; the corners were taken first, mostly by local business owners.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: It sits in Cameron Centrum, an 87-acre township beside Brinchang by the developer of the older Brinchang Square, alongside a stratified commercial centre, the short-stay apartments of Centrum Iris, a planned events hall and semi-detached commercial lots. A river separates Caspia from Iris, and the developer is landscaping walkways along it. The township's roads are the widest in Cameron Highlands, which draws about 1.3 million visitors a year.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Ground-floor shops in the existing Centrum rent for about RM8,000 to RM12,000 a month, against about RM5,000 in old Brinchang town. The developer's estimate for Caspia is about RM8,000 for each ground floor and RM4,000 for the top floor, where a normal three-storey shop office might fetch RM8,000, RM4,000 and RM2,500.

standout.title: Two ground floors on one lot
standout.body: Because the site slopes, each shop office opens at street level on both its front and its back, one floor apart, so it has two of the floors that earn the most rent and two frontages to advertise on. Sean doubts it could be done on flat land, and calls the township a demonstration of how to design commercial buildings.

pros: The master plan: an 87-acre township is rare in this location, and each phase adds something, from the shops with frontage on both sides to short-stay apartments, an events hall and now individual-title lots, so visitors can park once and spend the evening inside the township.

The use of the topography: two ground floors instead of one roughly doubles the most valuable space, giving estimated rents of RM8,000, RM8,000 and RM4,000 rather than the usual RM8,000, RM4,000 and RM2,500.

Individual title in limited numbers: the only shop lots in the township with no maintenance fee, suiting owners who want to run their own business or choose their own tenants, which is why the corner lots went first, mostly to locals.
cons: Only 24 units: a commercial area usually needs a critical mass of shops to draw people, so these only make sense as part of the wider master plan, not on their own.

Visibility: Caspia can't be seen from the main road into Cameron Highlands, one side faces the hill, and the other faces Centrum Iris across the river, so it relies on the developer's signage and on people already in the township.

Familiarity: buyers are either locals buying for their own business or investors going by the numbers, and visitors complain about traffic congestion, so investors should ask how long rents of RM8,000, RM8,000 and RM4,000 can last. Sean notes the township is also capturing local residents with banks, clinics and a grocer.

closing: A cleverly designed, maintenance-free shop office for local business owners and investors who believe in Cameron Centrum's crowds.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this July 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. The developer's team showed Sean the township and sales gallery; asking prices and rent estimates are the team's figures as he quoted them.
